## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | MEDIUM |
| Task type | correctness remediation |
| Complexity | STANDARD |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #195 reports that attached short-option detection is not scoped to the package manager. Yarn and Bun script arguments such as `-rfoo` can be mistaken for package selectors, causing valid tracked verification commands to fail preflight.

### What We Found

`packageScriptName` recognizes four package managers, then `assertNoPackageManagerOptions` rejects every hyphen-prefixed argument after `test`, `run`, or `run-script`, regardless of manager or whether the argument is already in the script-argument portion of the command. Thus `yarn run build -rfoo` is rejected even though Yarn forwards that argument to `build`; Bun has the same untested boundary. Existing tests cover npm selector attempts but do not cover attached short arguments for non-pnpm managers.

### Root Cause

Package-manager option detection is implemented as a manager-agnostic `argument.startsWith("-")` predicate. It conflates package selectors/options recognized by a specific manager with arbitrary script arguments and does not model the manager-specific script boundary.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Scope package-selector detection to the recognized manager and preserve valid Yarn/Bun script arguments. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Add focused regression coverage for accepted Yarn/Bun attached short arguments and rejected package selectors. |

### Evidence

- `packageScriptName` recognizes `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `bun` by executable basename.
- `assertNoPackageManagerOptions` currently rejects any argument beginning with `-` after the package command, with only `--` ending the scan.
- A command shaped as `["yarn", "run", "build", "-rfoo"]` therefore fails before `assertPackageScript` can validate the `build` script.
- Package-script validation reads `package.json` from the configured cwd, so selector-like package-manager arguments cannot be allowed indiscriminately.

### History Findings

- Issue #195 is a review-finding remediation from PR #192 and cites source issue #111.
- The current implementation added broad package-manager option rejection to prevent selectors from bypassing configured package cwd metadata.
- No repository test currently establishes manager-specific attached short-option behavior for Yarn or Bun.

### Recommendation

Introduce a small package-manager-specific selector predicate at the existing preflight boundary. Keep npm and pnpm selector/options rejection fail-closed, recognize only the selectors supported by Yarn/Bun (including their `--cwd` forms), and allow non-selector arguments after the script boundary where those managers forward them to the script. Add focused fixture-backed tests for accepted `yarn run build -rfoo` and Bun equivalents, plus rejection tests proving selectors remain blocked.

### Related Issues

- #111
- #192

### Decomposition Assessment

**Required**: no — this is a bounded parser/preflight correction with one implementation file and one focused test file.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Reproduce the reported Yarn/Bun attached short-option behavior against the current integration branch.
- [ ] Scope package-selector detection to the package manager without weakening configured-cwd package validation.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage for valid script arguments and rejected selectors.
- [ ] Run the required `check` verification and re-review the exact remediation head.
